claim: GM1 vesicles inhibit alpha-syn aggregation at neutral pH (opposite of pH 5.5)
source_quote: The opposite effect has been reported in studies conducted at neutral pH, where GM1 containing vesicles were found to inhibit aggregation [67] (Gaspar); The opposite effect has been reported for alpha-syn, pH 7.5, in the presence of lipid model membranes containing ganglioside (57) (Grey)
note: Corroborates Martinez 2007 direction (inhibition) and locates it at neutral pH. Treated as supporting context, not a primary measured record.

claim: DMPC (C14:0 PC) strongly SUPPRESSES alpha-syn aggregation, whereas DPPC (C16:0 PC) does not
source_quote: Dou and co-workers previously reported that the presence of LUVs composed of C14:0 PC (DMPC) strongly suppressed alpha-Syn aggregation ... such effects were not observed for DPPC
note: PRIORITY download: the Dou et al. primary paper has the DMPC suppression ThT data (DMPC is a candidate). Shows a 2-carbon change (14:0 fluid -> 16:0 gel) flips PC from suppressor to inert.

claim: Cholesterol enhances alpha-syn-membrane interaction, accelerating aggregation
asserted_in: matveyenka2024 (citing Jakubec et al., ref 35) + own data
source_quote: Jakubec and co-workers found that in lipid membranes, cholesterol (Cho) enhances protein-membrane interactions. This results in acceleration of alpha-Syn aggregation
note: Supports the matveyenka2024 primary finding that 60% cholesterol accelerates (via increased membrane hydrophobicity), contradicting a naive 'cholesterol orders membranes -> protective' view.
